paragraphs: The development environment setup for Chapter 4 of the micro-project involves configuring the necessary tools and libraries to develop the plant monitoring system using the arduino_stm32core framework. The project utilizes the ST-Link V2 via SWD interface for programming the STM32 microcontroller.

The code stats indicate that the plant_monitor.ino file contains 96 lines of code, with 61 of those being actual code lines. The framework used is arduino_stm32core, which builds upon the STM32 HAL drivers and provides a comprehensive set of functions for interacting with various peripherals.

The project requires specific hardware components to function correctly. These include an ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) connected to PA0 (ADC1_IN0), an active buzzer driver on PA1, an onboard status LED on PC13, and an USB-to-UART adapter for serial communication.

The system clock is set to 72 MHz with a PLL x9 configuration. The APB1 and APB2 prescalers are set to /2 and /1 respectively, and the ADC prescaler is set to /6. This setup ensures that the system operates efficiently with minimal power consumption.

To eliminate sensor measurement noise, the plant_monitor.ino file includes a moving average filtering function in the readSoilMoistureAverage function. This helps smooth out any fluctuations in soil moisture readings and provides more reliable data for further processing.

The onboard status LED on PC13 is configured as an active-low logic driver. To ensure that the indicator lights up when action is needed, a high-to-low transition from PA1 (active buzzer alert) to PC13 (onboard status LED) is used in the updateDisplay function.

To handle inverted active-low onboard indicator logic on PC13, the plant_monitor.ino file includes a conditional statement that checks if the value of PA1 is low and sets the state of PC13 accordingly. This ensures that the indicator lights up when action is needed.

The threshold or hysteresis state evaluation in the updateDisplay function helps prevent spurious state switching. When the soil moisture level falls below a certain threshold, the active buzzer alert on PA1 is turned off and the onboard status LED on PC13 is turned on. This prevents the indicator from flashing unnecessarily.
Overall, the development environment setup for Chapter 4 of the micro-project is well-organized and leverages the arduino_stm32core framework to create a reliable plant monitoring system.
